records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:12 — With retries disabled and no per-item error isolation, one malformed feed item aborts the whole poll and prevents every later item from importing.
records.rationale: The diff shows `sidekiq_options retry: false` in poll_feed.rb and the `rss.items.each` loop has no per-item error handling. A single malformed item (e.g., nil `i.content` causing `i.content.scrub` to raise, or an invalid item failing `TopicEmbed.import`) raises out of the loop, aborting the iteration so all subsequent feed items are skipped, and the failed run won't be retried. Mechanism verifiable in the diff.

records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:28 — Iterates and imports every feed item without a limit or incremental cursor, so a large feed causes unbounded work on every hourly poll.
records.rationale: Verified in the diff: poll_feed.rb does `rss.items.each` and calls `TopicEmbed.import` for every item with no limit, cursor, or use of the already-computed feed_key cache (feed_key is defined but never used to track feed modification). Each hourly run re-fetches and re-processes the entire feed. Existing embeds are skipped via the embed_url lookup, so it's not unbounded topic creation, but repeated full-feed processing per poll with an unused feed_key is a real, specific design concern grounded in this diff.

records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — Feed-supplied HTML is persisted with the raw_html cook method, so an untrusted feed entry can store executable markup and XSS every topic viewer.
records.rationale: The diff shows TopicEmbed.import creates posts with cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html], and Post#cook returns raw unmodified for that method, so feed-supplied HTML (PollFeed reads an arbitrary RSS feed's i.content and passes it to import) is persisted and rendered via `raw post.cooked` in embed/best.html.erb with no sanitization. Any script injected into the polled feed's content executes for embed viewers. The mechanism is verifiable in the diff; whether it's exploitable depends on trusting the feed source, so moderate confidence.

records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — Imported RSS content is persisted and rendered as raw HTML without sanitization, so malicious feed content can execute script in the forum origin.
records.rationale: TopicEmbed.import passes feed content through PostCreator with cook_method: raw_html, and Post#cook returns raw unchanged for that method ('return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]'). The only transformation is absolutize_urls, which only rewrites href/src attributes — no sanitization. The best.html.erb view renders it with 'raw post.cooked', executing in the forum origin. Malicious feed content (e.g., <script> in RSS content) would be stored and executed unsanitized.

records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — Passing the full Referer URL as postMessage targetOrigin rejects normal embedding pages with a path, so the public resize protocol never reaches its caller.
records.rationale: The diff line is `parent.postMessage({type: 'discourse-resize', height: ...}, '<%= request.referer %>')`. postMessage's targetOrigin is specified as a URL: per the HTML spec, when a full URL is supplied, only its origin is extracted and compared. So a referer containing a path (e.g. `http://host/article/123`) is still a valid targetOrigin and the message is delivered to the parent window's origin. records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — Defaulting `cook_method` to `raw_html` makes every newly created post bypass HTML sanitization, enabling stored XSS for ordinary users.
records.rationale: The migration sets `cook_method` default to 1: `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. Discourse's `Enum` (used in `Post.cook_methods`, i.e. `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`) is 1-indexed, so 1 maps to `:regular` and only 2 maps to `:raw_html`. The cook override explicitly checks `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, so ordinary posts (default 1 = regular) still go through the normal cooking pipeline. The finding's premise that the default is `raw_html` is factually wrong.
